steps.why: The two sheets overlap in early Dec 2010, so some rows appear twice.
Invoices starting with 'C' are returns. They would subtract from revenue and confuse order counts, so they live in their own table.
POST, DOT, M, D, BANK CHARGES, AMAZONFEE, ADJUST, TEST001, gift vouchers... are fees or bookkeeping lines, not products.
Negative quantities on non-cancel invoices are stock adjustments ('damaged', 'lost'), not purchases.
Free items and manual adjustments carry no revenue information.
e.g. a 'car flag' normally £1.7 listed at £1,157. Cheap furniture at £125+ is not removed because its median is also high.
Both such lines (74,215 jars, 80,995 birdies) were cancelled the same day and would add £245k of fake revenue.

checks.check: No missing invoice, stock code, date, quantity, price or country in sales
Every sale has quantity > 0 and unit price > 0
revenue = quantity x unit price (to the penny)
No invoice starts with 'C' in sales (cancellations live in returns)
Every stock code looks like a product code
Every sold stock code has a product record
No invoice is split across two customers
Dates fall inside the dataset's published range (Dec 2009 - Dec 2011)
No sale line above the extreme-quantity limit
